key_insight: Retrieval strategy (simple grep, dense/vector, or hybrid) strongly interacts with agent architecture and tool-calling design; the paper introduces a tailored 'Reshape' retrieval approach that, in many settings, yields better task success, efficiency, and robustness than naïve grep-only retrieval.
problem_solved: There is no systematic understanding or practical guidance for how retrieval choices affect performance of LLM agents that must call tools and reason over large corpora. The paper fills this gap by comparing retrieval strategies and showing when simple grep suffices and when more structured retrieval is required.
method: Propose 'Reshape' — a retrieval strategy that adapts signals and chunking to agent context and tool-call semantics (hybridizing sparse and dense cues).
Run systematic benchmarks across multiple agent architectures and tool-calling paradigms, measuring task success, latency, cost, and robustness.
Perform ablations and qualitative analyses to identify failure modes and provide practical guidelines for retrieval design in agentic systems.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners concrete, empirically grounded guidance for choosing retrieval designs for LLM agents—helping to trade off accuracy, latency, and cost and to decide when simple grep-like search is sufficient versus when to use advanced/hybrid retrieval.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: agent loop showing LLM, retrieval layer (grep vs vector vs Reshape), and tool-call interface.
Bar/line charts: comparative metrics (task success, latency, cost) for retrieval strategies across agent architectures.
Decision flowchart: when to use grep-only, dense retrieval, or Reshape based on task type, corpus size, and tool complexity.
Ablation table/heatmap: which components of Reshape contribute most to performance across scenarios.
paper_title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
paper_authors: Sahil Sen, Akhil Kasturi, Elias Lumer, Anmol Gulati, Vamse Kumar Subbiah
